channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Wealth Tax: Who Might Be Affected?
item.description: Kazakhstan is considering a wealth tax, potentially impacting families with mortgages and small businesses. Expert Maxim Baryshev suggests linking the tax to the Monthly Calculated Index (MCI) and adjusting for inflation to avoid penalizing average earners. The proposal aims to tax large assets and non-labor income.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Capital Market Development Program Aims to Boost Economy
item.description: Kazakhstan's capital market has nearly doubled in five years, but its role in financing the economy needs expansion. A new program aims to increase the use of exchange instruments by private enterprises, mobilizing additional funding sources for investment and modernization. The goal is to enhance the capital market's role in the national economy.

item.title: Bishkek CHPP Reports Equipment Readiness Amidst Normal Operations
item.description: The Bishkek Heating and Power Plant (CHPP) is operating normally, with its main equipment functioning according to technological parameters. The plant reported an average electrical capacity of 223 megawatts, utilizing 6 boiler units and 4 turbine units, with 8 boiler and 3 turbine units in reserve. No accidents or malfunctions have been reported.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Hydropower Potential for Ancillary Services Highlighted by EDBR
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's hydroelectric power plants (HPPs) can generate additional revenue beyond electricity sales by providing grid regulation services to neighboring countries. The Eurasian Development Bank (EDB) notes significant untapped potential in hydropower flexibility, crucial for stabilizing grids with growing solar and wind power. EDB suggests separate payment for these services.

item.title: Eurasian Development Bank Warns of Declining Water Levels in Toktogul Reservoir
item.description: The Eurasian Development Bank (EDB) expresses concern over decreasing water levels in Kyrgyzstan's Toktogul Reservoir amid rising electricity consumption. Experts note critical low water levels, impacting both electricity generation and agricultural irrigation. EDB suggests closer regional energy cooperation to optimize water resource use and secure electricity imports.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Criticized for Violating Election Campaign Rules
item.description: The President of Kyrgyzstan has faced criticism for allegedly violating election campaign rules. The article poses the question of what his response to these accusations might be, indicating a public discussion or controversy surrounding his campaign conduct.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Residents Urge President to Halt Gold Mining in Tourist Zone
item.description: Residents of Aksy district, Kyrgyzstan, have appealed to President Sadyr Japarov to stop gold mining licenses issued in a tourist zone. They fear damage to tourism, water sources, and nature. An independent environmental commission has submitted its findings to the district administration.

item.title: Afghanistan Seeks Stronger Standards Cooperation with Turkey and Regional Partners
item.description: Afghanistan's Standard and Quality Authority (ASQA) has held talks with counterparts from Turkey, Uzbekistan, Saudi Arabia, and Kazakhstan to enhance technical cooperation and strengthen its standards infrastructure. Discussions included employee training, quality certification, and laboratory services.

item.title: Central Asia Faces Growing Electricity Deficit by 2030, EDB Warns
item.description: Electricity demand in Central Asia is projected to increase by 27% by 2030, according to Arman Akhunbaev of the Eurasian Development Bank. This growth, driven by industrial development and urbanization, could lead to an energy deficit if power capacities and grids are not modernized. The EDB emphasizes the need for simultaneous upgrades to transmission lines and energy storage systems.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans to Allocate 6.5 Trillion Tenge from National Fund for Infrastructure
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to allocate approximately 6.5 trillion tenge from the National Fund by the end of 2029 to modernize social, transport, and engineering infrastructure. Funds will be used for constructing hospitals, maternity wards, schools, cultural facilities, and providing drinking water and gas to settlements. Economists are assessing the impact on prices, the tenge exchange rate, and the fund's future.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee Investigates Former Zhanaozen Mayor
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee has confirmed a pre-trial investigation into Zhanseit Kainarbaev, the former mayor of Zhanaozen. The committee has not disclosed the specific case for which he is suspected. Social media had previously reported his detention and possible involvement in a kidnapping case.

item.title: Verdict Overturned for Former Deputy Head of Shymkent National Security Committee
item.description: The verdict against the former deputy head of the Shymkent branch of the National Security Committee (KNB) has been overturned. No further details regarding the case or the reasons for the verdict's annulment were provided.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee Confirms Investigation into Former Zhanaozen Akim
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee has confirmed a pre-trial investigation into Zhanseit Kainarbaev, the former Akim of Zhanaozen. While the specific suspicions remain undisclosed, reports suggest the investigation is related to alleged kidnapping. Kainarbaev served as Akim from February 2024 to September 2026 before being appointed Akim of the Karaqiya district.

item.title: Man Sentenced to 8 Years in Aktobe for Wife's Death After Assault
item.description: A 40-year-old man in Aktobe has been sentenced to eight years in prison for the death of his common-law wife following an assault. The prosecution stated the man beat the victim out of jealousy and delayed calling for medical assistance. The victim died eight days later in intensive care due to a severe head injury caused by the blows, not a fall as the accused claimed.

item.title: Afghan UN Envoy Urges International Action on Human Rights, Women's Rights
item.description: Afghanistan's UN Representative Nasir Ahmad Faiq called for urgent international action to improve human rights in Afghanistan, particularly for women and girls. He stressed restoring rights to education and work, protecting vulnerable groups, and supporting migrants. Faiq also emphasized accountability for violations and meaningful participation of Afghans in decisions.

item.title: Online Casino Scheme with Over 188 Billion Tenge Turnover Uncovered in Astana
item.description: Authorities in Astana have concluded an investigation into an illegal online casino operation that processed over 188 billion tenge. Two suspects are in custody, three are out on bail, and two are under travel restrictions. The case involved a complex payment infrastructure using banks, payment organizations, and cryptocurrency to launder illicit funds.

item.title: Tajikistan: Khorog faces shortage of Russian-language classes for returning migrant children
item.description: Schools in Khorog, Tajikistan, lack sufficient Russian-language classes and teachers for children of migrants returning from Russia or unable to enroll there. Some children are placed in Tajik-language classes, causing adaptation difficulties. Authorities are considering expanding Russian-language education but face a shortage of qualified teachers.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Online casino organizers investigated for handling over $400 million
item.description: Kazakhstan's financial monitoring agency has concluded an investigation into organizers of online casinos, who allegedly processed over 188 billion tenge (approx. $400 million). The scheme involved bank sector representatives and disguised operations as legal betting. Assets worth 1.4 billion tenge, including crypto, have been seized.

item.title: Kazakhstan introduces three-year bachelor's degree programs in universities
item.description: Kazakhstan has legally enabled universities to offer bachelor's programs in three years. This change focuses on efficient academic scheduling rather than reducing the curriculum's scope. The number of academic credits remains the same, requiring 240 credits, or up to 300 for some fields. This system is already used by over 16,000 students.

item.title: Tajikistan Discusses Implementation of Four Strategic Documents
item.description: An interdepartmental working group met on October 28, 2026, at the Ministry of Economic Development and Trade of Tajikistan to discuss the implementation of four strategic planning documents. These include plans for social protection, artificial intelligence development, scientific research, and public finance management.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Amend Civil Code, Focusing on Future Economy
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Justice has proposed significant amendments to the Civil Code, aiming to create a foundation for the future economy. Key focuses include preserving effective private law institutions, strengthening property rights protection, ensuring contract reliability, and promoting freedom of contract with minimal state intervention.

item.title: 172,000 Uzbeks Returning from Abroad Employed in Nine Months, Ministry Reports
item.description: In the first nine months of the year, 172,000 Uzbek citizens returning from abroad were permanently employed, according to the Ministry of Employment. An additional 34,000 became self-employed entrepreneurs. The ministry's report highlights efforts to reintegrate returning migrants into the domestic workforce.

item.title: Rawadari Expresses Concerns Over ICC's Decision to Separate Afghanistan Investigation
item.description: Rawadari has voiced concerns that the International Criminal Court's decision to separate the Afghanistan investigation could complicate victims' access to justice and erode trust. The organization seeks clear explanations regarding the legal and practical implications of this separate probe.

item.title: Trump's Vice President Sends Letter to Iran on Nuclear Negotiations
item.description: US official JD Vance, serving as Vice President, sent a letter to Iran's Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei, emphasizing that any negotiations must include the nuclear issue. The letter was reportedly sent as President Trump considers resuming military operations against Iran.

item.title: Kazakhstan Government Tasked with Accelerating Energy Projects and Reducing Water Losses
item.description: The Kazakhstan government has been instructed to develop measures by December 15 to boost the mining and metallurgical sector, including the use of offtake contracts. The 'People's Construction' program aims to identify regional infrastructure and social facility needs by year-end. Domestic materials and equipment are prioritized for construction projects.

item.title: Kazakhstan Enhances Cybersecurity for Businesses Amid Digitalization
item.description: Kazakhstan is increasing personal data and financial system protection as digitalization accelerates. Cybersecurity requirements are expanding beyond government and banks to include small and medium-sized businesses. Experts suggest that meeting these demands is manageable with proper assessment of protection needs, as discussed at KazHackStan 2026.

item.title: Ten Drug Smugglers Killed in Clash with Tajik Border Guards in Takhar
item.description: Local sources reported that ten drug smugglers from Takhar province's Chah Ab district were killed in an armed confrontation with Tajikistan's border guards. The incident occurred on October 27, 2026, near the border in the Sarchashma and Qowaq areas. The smugglers were reportedly transporting drugs illegally when the clash began.

item.title: NVIDIA Unveils AI Model Capable of Recognizing Speech in 40 Languages
item.description: NVIDIA has introduced Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, an AI model designed for speech recognition, translation, and audio analysis. It supports 40 languages, including Turkish, and can process audio up to an hour long. The model can differentiate up to eight speakers in conversations and adapt to professional terminology.

item.title: Over 600 Drones Launched Towards Moscow, Airport Operations Limited
item.description: More than 600 drones were reportedly launched towards Moscow, leading to restrictions on operations at three airports. One of Bashkortostan's largest chemical plants, which produces terephthaloyl chloride used for military purposes, was also targeted.

item.title: UN Report: Afghanistan Opium Cultivation Surges 325% in 2026
item.description: Afghanistan's opium poppy cultivation has surged by 325% in 2026, according to a UN report. An estimated 43,300 hectares were planted, up from 10,200 hectares in 2025. Opium production also increased nearly fivefold to 1,466 tons.

item.title: 18-Year-Old Arrested for Alleged Murder of Fellow Villager in Hissar
item.description: An 18-year-old man has been arrested in Hissar on suspicion of murdering a fellow villager. The Ministry of Internal Affairs identified the suspect as Davronjon Umarov, who allegedly stabbed the victim, Salohiddin Kurbonov, during an argument on October 27.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Reduce Reporting Requirements for Teachers
item.description: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov has ordered a review and reduction of reporting duties for teachers to improve educational efficiency and reduce non-core workloads. The Ministry of Education, in collaboration with regional authorities, is tasked with eliminating duplicate reports and simplifying the process. Proposals to protect teachers' honor and dignity are also due by December 10.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Online Casino Organizers Face Trial Over Alleged Billions in Transactions
item.description: Kazakh authorities have transferred a case against alleged organizers of illegal online casinos, including Nomadgames and Sultangames, to court. The scheme allegedly involved bank sector representatives facilitating payment infrastructure, processing over 188 billion tenge. Funds were laundered through a controlled company and converted to cryptocurrency. Assets seized include properties, vehicles, and cash.

item.title: Tajikistan's National Bank and IMF Discuss Monetary Policy Enhancements
item.description: The National Bank of Tajikistan and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) concluded a technical assistance mission focused on improving monetary policy implementation. Discussions covered assessments of current mechanisms, tool effectiveness, and priorities for liquidity management and money market development. The collaboration aims to modernize Tajikistan's monetary policy tools.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Freedom Holding to Invest Over $230 Million in Intelligent Road Monitoring System
item.description: Freedom Holding Corp. will invest over 112 billion tenge (approximately $230 million) through its subsidiary Freedom Lab to build an Intelligent Road Monitoring System (IRMS). The agreement was signed with Kazakhstan's Ministry of Transport. The system will use automatic measuring stations to record vehicle weight and dimensions, transmitting data to a unified system for analysis.

item.title: Kazakhstan Prime Minister Orders Increase in Primary Healthcare Physician Salaries
item.description: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov has ordered a salary increase of up to 40% for primary healthcare physicians and medical staff, effective January 1st. The government plans to allocate funds for this in the three-year budget. He also emphasized the need to modernize primary healthcare and focus on disease prevention and early detection.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Soft Drink Association Criticizes Sugar Import Quotas
item.description: The Uzbekistan Association of Non-Alcoholic Drinks and Juices opposes the planned introduction of a 300,000-ton annual quota on white sugar imports starting in 2027. The association argues this will increase raw material costs, production expenses, and inflation.

item.title: Kazakh Prime Minister Explains Reason for Samruk-Energy Head's Dismissal
item.description: Kazakh Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov stated that the former head of Samruk-Energy, Kairat Maksutov, was dismissed for ignoring warnings regarding delays in energy projects. Maksutov was repeatedly cautioned about the slow progress of strategic investment projects, including the modernization of Almaty's third thermal power plant.

item.title: Uzbekistan plans tax exemptions for transport infrastructure and new buses
item.description: Uzbekistan is planning tax and customs benefits for transport infrastructure and new buses. New buses meeting Euro-5 standards will be exempt from utilization fees until December 2027. Bus stations, railway stations, and airports will be exempt from property and land taxes from 2027 to 2030.

item.title: Czech archaeologists excavate Soviet-era Gulag camp ruins in Kazakhstan
item.description: Czech organization Gulag.cz, in collaboration with archaeologists from the University of West Bohemia, has excavated the remains of the Steplag Gulag camp in Kazakhstan. This marks the first such research in a post-Soviet country. The site includes ruins of male and female camps, guard housing, and a victims' cemetery, offering unique insights into the Soviet penal system.
